summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma was admitted for Cycle 33 of scheduled methotrexate chemotherapy. He reported feeling well since his recent outpatient ureteral stent removal and denied fevers, shortness of breath, nausea, or rashes. His hospital course was uncomplicated; he received methotrexate and temozolomide with leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate per protocol, tolerating treatment with only mild nausea. Methotrexate levels decreased appropriately, falling to 0.12 by discharge. His sodium was mildly low at 128 but stable, and creatinine remained normal at 1.0. Lisinopril, which had been held during a prior admission, was restarted given stable renal function. He was discharged home on oral sodium bicarbonate to continue until his next oncology visit in four months, with all other medications resumed as before. Follow-up was scheduled with neuro-oncology.
problems: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, extranodal and solid organ sites
